clue.text: A threesome firmly quashed — loser, big time!

indicators.note: quashed means crushed out of shape, so the letters of these three words are squashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone groans at a firm refusal of a three-in-bed proposal and calls the would-be lover a huge loser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loser, big time' reads as an insult, but the loser here is a dieter who has shed the most weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The title goes to the dieter who sheds the most weight in a year, a champion at losing in a big way.

clue.text: Fix fight closer to time

parts.note: a scrap is a brawl or scuffle

indicators.note: the closer of a word is its final letter, here the end of time

explanation.surface: An instruction to rig a boxing match so the fight ends near the time limit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fix is a tight spot or predicament, and so is a scrape, as in getting into scrapes.

clue.text: One's smart about working — I wish it were true

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is read as 'has' and links

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for smart surrounds the word for working

parts.note: fly is slang for sharp or streetwise
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone longs to be clever about their job, sighing that they wish it were so.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of wistful longing, saying the same as wishing something were the case.

clue.text: Cattle Mike flogged for financial security

indicators.note: flogged means beaten, so the letters of these two words are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A farmer called Mike sold his cattle to give himself a financial cushion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flogged' looks like British slang for sold, which suits the farm picture, but it is beating the letters into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A source of steady income or support that someone relies on is called this, often a person exploited for money.

clue.text: Get to be moralistic when out of power

indicators.note: out of means without, so the letter for power is taken away

parts.note: to preach is to moralise at people
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A complaint about a deposed politician who has started lecturing people now that office is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to a place is to arrive there, the same as reaching it.

clue.text: Particular recollection of cool drinks coming round

indicators.note: a recollection looks back, so the whole assembly is read from the end
the drinks word comes round, enclosing the word for cool

parts.note: an animal laps when it drinks
to ice something is to chill or cool it

explanation.surface: Someone fondly remembers a particular round of chilled drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion gives LAICEPS, which 'recollection of' reads from the end; 'drinks' is a verb here, as a cat lapping milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Particular and this word are both adjectives meaning specific or distinct from the rest.

clue.text: Local issue that's not serious

definitions.meaning: a local is a British pub, and weak beer is something it issues to customers

explanation.surface: A council matter that nobody needs to worry about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local issue' looks like parish politics; a local is a British neighbourhood pub, and what it issues is beer, here the weak kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak beer once served cheaply came to stand for anything trivial or unimportant.

clue.text: Point out emperor's a god

indicators.note: out means dropped, so the compass letter leaves the emperor's name

parts.note: Nero was the Roman emperor, and his possessive gives the letters with S
N is north, one of the compass points

explanation.surface: Someone points out that a Roman emperor was worshipped as a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love, son of Aphrodite, is a deity, the counterpart of Roman Cupid.

clue.text: Vice beginning to increase in New York — I'm going!

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of increase
in places the quitting statement inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: a person leaving announces 'I quit'

explanation.surface: Someone appalled by rising crime in New York announces they are leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice and this word both mean wickedness or a grossly immoral act.

clue.text: Occasionally subdued after making love below lecturer's room

indicators.note: in a down answer, below puts the lovemaking phrase under the lecturer's letter
after puts the picked letters following the lovemaking phrase

parts.note: L is a standard abbreviation for lecturer
a couple who are at it are having sex, a British idiom

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of subdued is used

explanation.surface: A rather subdued couple have sex in the room below a lecturer's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' takes the even letters of subdued, U, D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Room in the sense of freedom or scope to act is exactly what this word means.

clue.text: Woman around hotel bar's one

indicators.note: the bar word goes around the hotel letter

parts.note: a rod is a bar; the 's links
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A woman is drinking somewhere near a hotel bar.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female given name, so any woman bearing it fits.

clue.text: It's very small at first, doctor

parts.note: an atom is a thing that is very small
first is abbreviated 1ST, with the figure read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A patient tells the doctor that a growth was very small at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of the abbreviation 1st is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist in the structure of the body, typically medically trained, is one kind of doctor.

clue.text: Traveller in the main story sounding keen to tour India

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the story word circles the India letter

parts.note: the plot of a story is its storyline
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: sounding says the word for keen is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: to keen is to wail in mourning

explanation.surface: A travel writer's story makes them sound eager for a trip around India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the open sea, and keen is the verb for crying out in grief, not the adjective eager.
explanation.definitionFit: This marine mammal journeys through the ocean, which older poetry calls the main.

clue.text: Thousands spent by top clubs?

indicators.note: the thousands are used up, so they go from the word for top

parts.note: the summit is the top of a mountain
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them make MM

explanation.surface: A question about the big money spent by Premier League football clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: clubs is one of the four card groups.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs is one of the four card categories in a pack, alongside hearts, diamonds and spades.

clue.text: Vague about taking sweetheart back, with wife in such a state

indicators.note: the wife letter is set inside the rest
about means turned round, so the word for vague is read backwards

parts.note: dim means vague or hazy
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A man too vague to remember things takes his girlfriend back and marries her, then finds himself in a right state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In such a state' looks like flustered, but 'such a state' is a US state like Iowa or Ohio.
explanation.definitionFit: States such as Ohio, Iowa and Kansas belong to the central US region, so a state there is described this way.

clue.text: Mean to temper disc of steel

indicators.note: tempering steel works and reshapes it, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone means to harden a steel disc by tempering it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' reads as a verb, intend; it is the adjective stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean in the sense of stingy with money matches this word, which pictures a fist clenched round cash.

clue.text: See 1 across
Love to impale non-stop, being conscientious

indicators.note: impaling pierces right through, so the love letter is driven inside the other word

parts.note: a through train runs non-stop
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A violent picture of loving to skewer things without pause, as a mark of diligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful and complete in doing a job, leaving nothing out, as a conscientious worker is.

clue.text: Sure old rogue's carrying money to look sexy!

indicators.note: the jumbled letters carry the money letter within them
a rogue behaves wildly, and 'is rogue' tells these letters to run out of order

explanation.surface: An ageing rogue, flush with cash, is confident he looks sexy.
explanation.definitionFit: To smoulder is to show suppressed passion, giving off a sultry, seductive look.

clue.text: Fashion worth wearing in the event

parts.note: to hammer metal is to fashion it into shape

indicators.note: wearing wears the word down out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion that is worth wearing on the night in question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like clothing, but it is the verb, as a smith hammers metal into shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing a heavy ball on a wire is one athletics field contest, an event at meetings and the Olympics.

clue.text: Discussion about female in Hackney

indicators.note: the about and female letters go inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a hackney carriage is the official name for a London taxi
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A talk about a woman living in Hackney, an area of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney looks like the London borough, but a hackney carriage is a taxi, the black cab.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal chat or conversation is called this, short for confabulation.

clue.text: For one promoted, Horace's work rocks

indicators.note: in a down answer promotion moves up, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: EG, for example, means for one
the Roman poet Horace wrote odes

explanation.surface: A schoolboy promoted for his work on Horace finds it rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: These are hollow stones lined with crystals, so they are rocks.

clue.text: Rector's away on retreat

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rector; the 's is read as 'is' and links
someone who is out is away from home

explanation.surface: The vicar is absent, off on a spiritual retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' suggests a religious getaway; here it is a noun for an army's disorderly flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorderly retreat by a beaten army is a crushing defeat and flight, as in put to flight.

clue.text: Some games of short tennis arranged and unlikely to be changed

parts.note: a set in tennis is a group of games

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged
short means cut off at the end, so the last letter of 'of' goes

explanation.surface: A few games of short tennis are fixed and cannot be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' trims 'of' to O; 'arranged' rearranges O with TENNIS to give INSTONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carved into rock is permanent, so the idiom describes a fixed plan beyond change.

clue.text: Start, not finish, at site of siege

parts.note: at a place is in it

indicators.note: not finishing means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Troy was the city the Greeks besieged for ten years

explanation.surface: An unfinished start to a battle at a famous siege location.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction or opening passage of a song or talk is its start.

clue.text: Beer's always off — port or spirit?

indicators.note: off means removed, so the word for always comes away from the beer word

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A drinker finds the beer always off and wonders whether to try port or spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port or spirit' looks like a choice of drinks; port is a harbour city and spirit means verve.
explanation.definitionFit: This word means vigour or vivacity, the spirit someone shows in performing.

clue.text: Did suffer going round in that new red number

indicators.note: going round means turning back, so the found letters are read backwards
in says the letters lie inside these words

explanation.surface: Someone endured wearing that new red outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like an outfit, but it only supplies letters: reading T NEW RED NU backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something unpleasant is to go through or suffer it, here in the past tense.

clue.text: Swore what Emirates official did's not right

indicators.note: not means without, so the right letter goes

parts.note: an official at the Emirates, Arsenal's London football stadium, reffed, short for refereed, the match

explanation.surface: A football referee at the Emirates Stadium got something wrong and cursed.
explanation.walkthrough: Emirates looks like the Gulf state or airline, but it is the Emirates Stadium, Arsenal's home ground in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Effing is a euphemistic way of swearing, so this past tense means swore.

clue.text: Secretly maintain hotel's leafy area

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet; the 's links
an arbour is a shady garden bower of leaves

explanation.surface: Someone is quietly keeping up a hotel's garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour a grudge or suspicion is to keep it privately in mind.

clue.text: Old writer involved in problem over collected works

indicators.note: the writer word is wrapped inside the reversed problem word
over means turned over, so the word for problem is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: An old author wrestles with a problem in finishing a collected edition.
explanation.definitionFit: A single volume gathering several works by one author is an edition of this name.
